explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. The spies went into Jericho and stayed at the house of a woman named Rahab, and the text calls her a prostitute plainly. It doesn't say why they picked her door, so I won't guess. Keep her name handy, because she's about to be the hero of this whole chapter.

Naomi was a widow, friend, but she's from a different story. Her husband died and she was left with her two sons (Ruth 1:3). The spies in Jericho stayed with a woman named Rahab, who is described as a prostitute.

Lydia is a real woman in the Bible, a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira (Acts 16:14). But she shows up much later, in a whole other book. The spies in Jericho stayed with a woman named Rahab.

explanations.answer: Bring the men out to him
explanations.explanation: Right on the money. The king says, “Bring out the men who came to you and entered your house…” He says they came to spy out the whole land. Notice he sends the order straight to Rahab's door.

explanations.answer: Keep the men inside her house
explanations.explanation: The king wants the opposite of that. He doesn't want the spies tucked away anywhere. He tells Rahab to bring out the men who came to her and entered her house.

explanations.answer: Send the men out of town
explanations.explanation: That would be a gentle way to handle spies, and the king isn't gentle about it. He tells Rahab to bring the men out to him. His words are that they have come to spy out the whole land.

Not quite, friend. The text says the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. She tells the king's men the spies did come, but she never hands them over. So the answer is False, and the spies are still safe.

That's it. The woman had taken the two men and hidden them before the king's men ever knocked. She admits the men came to her, but she says she didn't know where they came from. The spies never leave her hands for the king's.
Yes, baker. She says, “Pursue them quickly, and you may catch them!” She sends the king's men running off after men who are really up on her roof. That's a whole lot of confidence in one sentence.

explanations.answer: Wait for them at the gate
explanations.explanation: Waiting at the gate isn't what she says. She tells them the men already went out at dusk, when the gate was about to close. Then she says, “Pursue them quickly, and you may catch them!”

That plan would have ended with somebody checking her roof, so it's good she didn't say it. She points the king's men away from town instead. Her words are, “Pursue them quickly, and you may catch them!”

True, friend. The king's men set out after the spies along the road to the fords of the Jordan, and as soon as they had gone out, the gate was shut. The timing is tight. The men on the road left, and the door closed right behind them.
It's True, friend. The text says that as soon as the king's men had gone out, the gate was shut. There's no gap in it. Out they go, and the gate closes.

explanations.answer: The LORD has given Israel the land
explanations.explanation: That's what she says. Rahab tells the spies, “I know that the LORD has given you this land…” She says it plainly, up on her own roof. Keep an ear out, because she's just getting warmed up.

explanations.answer: The king will find them by morning
explanations.explanation: She doesn't say a word about the king finding them. She's the one who sent his men off down the road. What she says up on the roof is, “I know that the LORD has given you this land…”

explanations.answer: Jericho's walls can never be broken
explanations.explanation: She says nothing about walls, baker. Her words are about the LORD and what He has done. She says, “I know that the LORD has given you this land…”

True. Rahab says the fear of Israel has fallen on them, “so that all who dwell in the land are melting in fear of you.” That's a strong picture, like a cookie left on a warm window ledge. She's telling them how the whole land feels.
It's True, friend. Rahab says the fear of them has fallen on the people, so that “all who dwell in the land are melting in fear of you.” The spies are about to take that same news back to Joshua.

Yes. Rahab says Israel devoted Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites across the Jordan, to destruction. That's part of what Jericho has heard. The news had traveled a long way before the spies ever got there.

explanations.answer: Made a peace treaty with them
explanations.explanation: No treaty in her story, friend. Rahab says Israel devoted Sihon and Og to destruction. They were the two kings of the Amorites across the Jordan.

explanations.answer: Let them flee across the river
explanations.explanation: That's not what she says. Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites across the Jordan, didn't get away in her telling. She says Israel devoted them to destruction.

explanations.answer: God in heaven above and on earth below
explanations.explanation: That's her exact point. Rahab says, “…for the LORD your God is God in the heavens above and on the earth below.” That's a big thing to say about God from a rooftop in Jericho. Her words, and I think they're worth slowing down for.

explanations.answer: God over Israel and no one else
explanations.explanation: She says something much bigger than that. Rahab doesn't limit Him to Israel. She says the LORD your God “is God in the heavens above and on the earth below.”

explanations.answer: The strongest of all the gods
explanations.explanation: She isn't ranking Him in a lineup, baker. She says He is God, in the heavens above and on the earth below. Her words are, “…for the LORD your God is God in the heavens above and on the earth below.”
Yes, family. She asks them to spare the lives of her father and mother, her brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them. That's her whole household. She wants them delivered from death.
Not the town, friend. Rahab asks for her family. She names her father and mother, her brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them.

The king is the one who sent men to catch the spies, so he's not on her list. She asks them to spare the lives of her family. That means her father and mother, her brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them.

True. The men agree, “Our lives for your lives!” They add, “If you do not report our mission, we will show you kindness and faithfulness when the LORD gives us the land.” So her silence is part of the deal.

It's True, friend. The spies say, “If you do not report our mission, we will show you kindness and faithfulness when the LORD gives us the land.” They start with “Our lives for your lives!” and the promise hangs on her keeping quiet.
That's right, baker. Her house is built into the city wall, so she let them down through the window by a rope. No front door and no street. I get nervous just standing on a counter edge.
No ladder here. The text says Rahab let them down through the window by a rope. Her house was built into the city wall, so the window was their way out.

A basket does show up for a wall escape in another story, where someone is lowered through an opening in the wall (Acts 9:25). But Rahab's spies went down by a rope. Her house was built into the wall, and the window was the way out.
Yes, the hill country. Rahab tells them to go there so their pursuers will not find them. She has the plan ready before they even reach the ground. That's one thoughtful host.
Ai is another city, and Rahab doesn't send them there. She says, “Go to the hill country…” She wants them somewhere their pursuers will not find them.
The wilderness of Zin is a desert region, but she doesn't name it. Her words are, “Go to the hill country…” She says it so their pursuers will not find them.
Yes. She says to hide there for three days until the pursuers have returned, and then go on their way. Her plan has a clear finish line. Hide, wait, and then go.
Rahab doesn't mention Joshua sending anyone. She says to hide for three days until the pursuers have returned. After that, they can go on their way.

explanations.answer: Until the gate opens at dawn
explanations.explanation: The gate isn't her marker. Rahab says to hide in the hill country for three days until the pursuers have returned. Only then do they go on their way.
That's it. The spies say she must tie this scarlet cord in the window she let them down through. It's one of their two conditions. A little red cord with a big job.
The text names a different thing. The spies tell her to tie a scarlet cord in the window through which she let them down. That's the first condition.
No tassel in this story, friend. The spies say she has to tie a scarlet cord in the window she let them down through. That's their first condition.
True. The spies say she must have brought her father and mother and brothers and all her family into her house. That's the second condition. The cord and the family both come before the oath holds.
It's True, friend. The spies say she must bring her father and mother and brothers and all her family into her house. That's the second condition. It goes alongside the scarlet cord.
That's right. Rahab says, “Let it be as you say.” No haggling, no extra rounds. She agrees and sends them away.
She doesn't ask for any more time, baker. Her answer is short, “Let it be as you say.” Then she sends them away.
No bargaining after this, friend. The text gives her one short answer, “Let it be as you say.” After that she sends them away.
Not this time, friend. The text says when the spies had gone, she tied the scarlet cord in the window. She didn't wait for Israel to arrive. So the answer is False.
Yes, False. Rahab said, “Let it be as you say,” and she sent them away. And when they had gone, she tied the scarlet cord in the window. She did it right then.

True. The spies stayed in the hill country three days, until their pursuers had returned without finding them. The pursuers had searched all along the road. They looked everywhere except where the spies were.
It's True, friend. The text says the pursuers returned without finding them, having searched all along the road. The spies stayed hidden in the hill country for three days.

explanations.answer: Delivered the entire land into their hands
explanations.explanation: Yes. The spies tell Joshua, “The LORD has surely delivered the entire land into our hands.” They add that all who dwell in the land are melting in fear of them. That's the same thing Rahab told them on the roof.

explanations.answer: Made Jericho's king surrender to them
explanations.explanation: They don't report anything like that. Jericho's king was still hunting for them. What they say is, “The LORD has surely delivered the entire land into our hands.”

explanations.answer: Sent them a sign in the night sky
explanations.explanation: No sign in the night sky in this report. The spies say, “The LORD has surely delivered the entire land into our hands.” Then they say that all who dwell in the land are melting in fear of them.
